name: Rongali (Bohag) Bihu
cultural_importance: The chief festival of Assam marking the onset of the agricultural seeding season and Assamese New Year. Youth perform energetic Bihu dances with Dhol, Pepa (buffalo horn flute), and Gogona, exchanging handwoven Gamusas as tokens of love and respect.

name: Bhogali (Magh) Bihu
cultural_importance: The harvest thanksgiving festival dedicated to the god of fire (Agni). Communities erect temporary thatch-and-bamboo pavilions (Meji & Bhelaghar) in fields, enjoy community feasts on Uruka night, and light the Meji at dawn.

name: Ambubachi Mela
cultural_importance: Celebrates the annual menstruation of Mother Earth and Goddess Kamakhya atop Nilachal Hill. Millions of sadhus, tantric practitioners, and pilgrims assemble at Kamakhya Temple during the four-day sanctum closure.
highlights: Distribution of Angodak & Raktavastra Sacred Cloth

name: Jonbeel Mela
cultural_importance: A 500-year-old historic barter fair where Tiwa, Karbi, Khasi, and Jaintia hill tribes descend to exchange ginger, hill chillies, and herbs for plains rice, fish, and cakes without using any money.
highlights: Community Fish Hunting in Jonbeel Lake

name: Ziro Festival of Music (ZFM)
cultural_importance: India's greatest outdoor eco-friendly indie music gathering, held amid the pine-covered paddy fields of Ziro Valley. All festival stages are built using local sustainable bamboo and pine.

name: Monpa Losar Festival
cultural_importance: The 15-day Monpa celebration of the Tibetan Buddhist New Year in Tawang and West Kameng, featuring monastic prayers, prayer flag hoisting, butter lamp illuminations, and colourful pantomime Aji Lhamu mask dances.
highlights: Raising of New Buddhist Prayer Flags

name: Dree Festival
cultural_importance: The most important agricultural festival of the Apatani tribe, where prayers are offered to gods Tamu, Harniang, Metii, and Danyi to protect crops from pests, famine, and hail.

name: Torgya Monastic Festival
period: January (28th day of 11th Monpa lunar month)
cultural_importance: A three-day annual monastic festival at Tawang Monastery to ward off evil spirits, ensure agricultural prosperity, and invoke blessings through sacred monastic masked dances.
highlights: Monk Orchestra with Long Alpine Horns

name: Wangala 100 Drums Festival
cultural_importance: The post-harvest thanksgiving festival of the Garo tribe, dedicated to Saljong, the Sun God of Fertility. A hundred drummers in feathered headgear play long oval drums (Dama) in rhythmic synchronized choreography.
highlights: Garo Warrior Dance in Feathered Turbans

name: Nongkrem Dance Festival
cultural_importance: A five-day annual Khasi thanksgiving dance at the royal court of the Syiem of Hima Khyrim in Smit to thank Almighty God (U Blei Nongthaw) for harvest and peace.
highlights: Unmarried Khasi Maidens in Gold Ornaments
Male Warriors with Silver Swords and Yak Whisks

name: Behdienkhlam Festival
cultural_importance: The most significant cultural festival of the Jaintia (Pnar) community in Jowai, aimed at driving away the plague of evil spirits and pestilence through ceremonial dancing in sacred muddy pools.

name: Shillong Autumn & Cherry Blossom Festival
cultural_importance: Celebrates the unique autumn blooming of wild Himalayan cherry blossom trees (Prunus cerasoides) alongside indie rock concerts, cosplay, fashion showcases, and street food.
highlights: Street Food and Craft Wine Stalls

name: Yaoshang (Manipuri Spring Festival)
cultural_importance: Manipur's version of Holi, celebrated over five vibrant days with the burning of the Yaoshang bamboo hut, traditional Thabal Chongba (dancing by moonlight holding hands), and grand community sports tournaments.

name: Manipur Sangai Festival
cultural_importance: The state's grand tourism extravaganza named after the rare Sangai deer, showcasing classical Manipuri Raas Leela dance, Sagol Kangjei (ancestral polo), indigenous martial arts (Thang-Ta), and handlooms.

name: Sajibu Nongma Panba (Cheiraoba)
cultural_importance: The traditional Meitei lunar New Year, where families clean their homes, prepare lavish feasts offered to household deities, and climb nearby sacred hillocks (Cheiraoching) to symbolize rising to greater heights in life.

name: Kang (Manipuri Rath Yatra)
cultural_importance: The ten-day chariot procession of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra starting at Shri Govindaji Temple, celebrated with devotional Jayadeva chants, bell ringing, and feasts of seasonal sweets.
highlights: Pulling of the Grand Timber Ratha Chariot
Devotional Sankirtana and Pung Cholom Drum Dance

name: Chapchar Kut Festival
cultural_importance: The most joyous festival of the Mizos, celebrated after the bamboo jhum clearing is completed. Men and women wear colourful traditional Puanchei shawls and perform the famous Cheraw bamboo dance to drumbeats.

name: Anthurium Tourism Festival
cultural_importance: Held amidst the blooming exotic red anthurium plantations at the foot of Reiek Mountain, highlighting floriculture, Mizo handloom weaving, archery, and fashion.
highlights: Rock Music and Acoustic Folk Shows

name: Thalfavang Kut
cultural_importance: Celebrated to mark the completion of weeding in the agricultural fields, bringing together various clans to perform folk dances like Khuallam, Chheihlam, and Tlanglam.

name: The Hornbill Festival
cultural_importance: The world-famous 'Festival of Festivals' organized by the Government of Nagaland, uniting all 16 recognized Naga tribes at Kisama Heritage Village to revive tribal traditions, crafts, and music.
highlights: All 16 Naga Tribal Dances in Full Warrior Regalia

name: Moatsu Mong Festival
cultural_importance: The premier spring festival of the Ao Naga tribe in Mokokchung, celebrated after the completion of field sowing with singing, dancing, tug-of-war, and recounting ancient heroic battle stories.

name: Sekrenyi (Phousanyi) Festival
cultural_importance: The Angami Naga purification festival celebrated to cleanse the body, soul, and village of all misfortunes and illness before the start of agricultural operations.
highlights: Ritual Morning Bathing at Sacred Village Springs

name: Aoleang Monyu Festival
cultural_importance: The chief festival of the Konyak Naga tribe in Mon, celebrating the arrival of spring and seeking blessings for a bumper crop with traditional gun-firing and ceremonial war dances.
highlights: Konyak War Dances with Traditional Muzzle-loading Guns

name: Kharchi Puja (Worship of Fourteen Gods)
cultural_importance: A centuries-old royal festival in Old Agartala where the Fourteen Dynastic Gods (Chaturdasha Devata) are worshipped and cleansed in the sacred Saidra (Howrah) River to purify the Earth after her menstruation.
highlights: River Procession of the Fourteen Golden Deities
Grand Fair with Bengali and Tribal Crafts

name: Garia Puja
cultural_importance: An ancient tribal festival of prosperity celebrated by the Tripuri, Reang, and Jamatia communities. A bamboo pole representing Lord Garia is worshipped with dancing, music, and chanting.
highlights: Garia Dance with Sacred Bamboo Staff
Community Prayers for Peace and Livestock

name: Saga Dawa
period: May / June (Full moon of 4th Tibetan month)
cultural_importance: The most sacred day in Tibetan Buddhism, commemorating the Birth, Enlightenment (Nirvana), and Parinirvana of Shakyamuni Buddha. Monks lead grand processions carrying sacred Kangyur scriptures through Gangtok.

name: Pang Lhabsol
period: August / September (15th day of 7th Tibetan month)
cultural_importance: Unique to Sikkim: commemorates the historic blood brotherhood treaty between the Lepcha and Bhutia tribes, and pays homage to Mount Kangchenjunga as the guardian deity of the realm.
